newsitem.title: USA: TWA sees unusual costs lower in Q2, Q3.
newsitem.headline: TWA sees unusual costs lower in Q2, Q3.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc said it expected its first-quarter loss and finished the period "ahead of plan," and it expects "unusual" costs to decline in the second and third quarters.

"First quarter results reflect certain unusual costs -- including an accelerated narrow-body maintenance schedule and training costs associated with the phase-out of our larger wide-body aircraft -- that will decline as we move into the second and third quarters," said chief executive Gerald Gitner.
TWA shares were up 3/8 to seven in early trading.
TWA reported quarterly revenue of $762.3 million, down from $782.4 million a year earlier. The airline lost $71.6 million on the quarter, compared with a year-ago loss of $37.1 million.

"The reduced revenue reflected a planned reduction in capacity resulting from the ongoing replacement of 747 and L1011 aircraft with smaller 767 and 757 aircraft. TWA also reduced the number of narrow-body aircraft in its schedule to move more aircraft through required scheduled maintenance prior to the peak travel season," TWA said.
Operating expenses for the quarter were $861.8 million, versus $836.6 million in the same period a year ago.
The average cost per gallon of jet fuel in the quarter was $0.7402, up from $0.6658 a year ago.

Quarterly revenue per available seat mile was $0.0875, up from $0.0831. Quarterly average yield per revenue passenger mile was $0.1184, up from $0.1159. Quarterly operating expense per available seat mile was $0.0986, compared with $0.0882.
Quarterly system-wide passenger load factor was 66.3 percent, up from 63.6 percent a year ago, TWA said.
